svg.title: How WIZARD learns to generate an adapter, and how it uses one
svg.desc: WIZARD architecture in two aligned bands. Meta-training, offline: a source task's instruction and video pass through the frozen pi0.5 encoder to a task representation, then the HyperConvVLA generator predicts an adapter and scale statistics. In parallel, the same task's action-labelled demonstrations train an expert LoRA adapter, whose weights are the training target for a reconstruction, scale and cosine loss. Deployment: a held-out instruction and one visual demonstration, with no action labels, go through the same frozen encoder and the same generator to produce an adapter, which is inserted into the frozen pi0.5 policy that drives the robot. Action labels never cross into deployment.
